stemMd: A competitive inhibitor reduces an enzyme reaction rate. Which change can reduce its effect while temperature and pH remain unchanged?

options.label: D
options.textMd: Replacing the enzyme with an unrelated protein

options.label: E
options.textMd: Adding more of the same inhibitor

explanationMd: A competitive inhibitor and the substrate compete for access to the active site. Raising substrate concentration makes substrate binding more likely and can overcome much of the inhibition. This reasoning applies to reversible competitive inhibition; it does not imply that more substrate reverses irreversible destruction of an enzyme.

distractorRationale.b: Less substrate leaves less competition against the inhibitor.
distractorRationale.e: More inhibitor increases competition for active sites.
distractorRationale.c: No catalysis remains when all enzyme is removed.
distractorRationale.d: An unrelated protein need not catalyse the reaction.
